va_3_mile_three.blurb: Mile Three is the third stop along Guest River Gorge in southwest Virginia, near Coeburn, with each stop marked by a mile signpost. The way in is a flat gravel rail bed, covered on foot or by bike, and it passes through an old coal train tunnel. Sport routes make up most of the climbing, with a set of boulders and a few trad lines alongside. Roped grades run from about 5.8 to 5.13, thickest from 5.10 through 5.13, and the boulder problems run from V2 to V8. Mile 3 Routes holds the most climbs, and Mile 3 Boulders holds the rest.

va_hidden_rocks.blurb: Hidden Rocks is a sandstone climbing area in the George Washington National Forest, roughly 15 miles southwest of Harrisonburg, Virginia. It mixes trad, sport, top-rope and bouldering, with trad holding the most routes. Roped grades run from about 5.4 to 5.12 and most sit in the 5.7 to 5.10 range, while the boulders are V0 to V2. Hidden Roofs is the newer, mainly sport area and holds the most climbs. Hidden Cracks and Lower Hidden are older crags with trad and top-rope lines, and Upper Lover's is a smaller sport and mixed crag.

wv_fern_buttress.blurb: Fern Buttress is a cliffline in West Virginia's New River Gorge, just downstream of Endless Wall. The rock is Nuttall sandstone, and the climbing is a mix of trad and sport, with trad making up the larger share. Grades are mostly 5.9 to 5.12, with a few 5.13s and some easier routes. Walls run in a row from Arm Forces Area to Fern Gully, and Ritz Cracker Area, Thieves Area and Orchard Wall hold the most climbs. Across the gorge the cliffs are described as hard, featured sandstone, and the best months are usually late April to mid-June and mid-September to late October.

wi_rib_mountain.blurb: Rib Mountain is a quartzite ridge standing above flat country in central Marathon County, Wisconsin, about four miles southwest of downtown Wausau. The climbing is nearly all bouldering on white quartzite, with most of it near the observation tower, and the problems come in many types and difficulties. Grades start at the easiest and mostly fall between V1 and V4, with only a few harder ones up to V7. Sixteen sub-areas are scattered around the ridge, and the Headstone Area and Jurassics hold the most climbs, followed by Smell the Moss and Ranger Station Rocks.

ca_cosumnes_river_gorge.blurb: Cosumnes River Gorge lies just outside Placerville, California, within reach of Sacramento. The rock is granite, worn smooth by water in places, and the climbing is varied: trad makes up the biggest share, alongside boulders, top-ropes and a little sport. Roped grades run from about 5.6 to 5.12, mostly 5.8 to 5.10, and the boulder problems range from V0 to V6. Buck's Bar Dome holds the most climbs, followed by Cosumnes River Bouldering, and Gutenberger Wall stands across the river. The gorge gets very hot in summer.

ca_fawnskin_area.blurb: The Fawnskin Area covers climbing west and north of the town of Fawnskin, in the San Bernardino Mountains near Big Bear Lake. Sport and trad share the routes about evenly, with some top-rope lines and almost no bouldering. Grades run from about 5.5 to 5.12, with 5.10 the most common and a good spread of moderates below it. The Coven holds the most climbs: its granite formations sit on a forested ridge with views over the lake, and the routes there tend to be on the shorter side. Legoland and Pinnacle with a View come next by climb count.
